newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia's 1997 winter rye output seen low.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia's 1997 winter rye output seen low.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA'S 1997 RYE OUTPUT SEEN LOWEST SINCE EARLY 1970s
MOSCOW, Feb 21 - Russian winter rye output in 1997 is provisionally forecast at 5.1 million tonnes -- or in a range between 4.6 and 5.6 million tonnes -- 14 percent down on 1996.
It would be the second lowest rye harvest (after 1995) since the early 1970s, and would mean Russia may become a small net-importer of rye in the 1997/98 season.
In the major Russian producing areas, winter rye plantings remain in generally satisfactory conditions.
Winter-kill losses are expected to be around 0.4 million hectares or 10 percent of winter rye acreage sown for the 1997 harvest, compared with 9 percent last year.
But the harvested winter rye area in 1997 is forecast to decline to about 3.5 million hectares, or 15 percent from 1996.
This reflects a serious drop in 1996 autumn sowings mainly resulting from financial constraints among producers.
Assuming normal crop development, winter rye yields are anticipated to be similar last year's levels in most areas.
